data.ru: линия блендирована: ширина в этом окне — это РАЗНОС, а не ширина линии (завышение ширины И правдоподобие второй компоненты): подгонка двумя гауссами даёт компоненты по 15.7 кэВ на расстоянии 0.84×ПШПВ компоненты при отношении высот 0.56, то есть одиночная ширина завышена в 1.74 раза (порог 1.45 без подтверждения, 1.15 с ним). Вторая компонента забирает Δchi2 = 53.4 на 2 параметра, то есть 7.17σ (пороги 3.5σ для снижения барьера разноса до 0.60 и 4.5σ для отказа по одному правдоподобию). ОТНОШЕНИЕ chi2 здесь молчит: одиночная подгонка даёт 2.56, выигрыш всего 1.14 раза — гладкая пара не портит chi2/dof, но забирает Δchi2 — ширина не имеет смысла
data.en: blended line: the width in this window reflects the separation of two components, not the width of a single line (the width is overestimated, and a second component is likely): a two-Gaussian fit gives components of 15.7 keV each, separated by 0.84 of the component FWHM, with a height ratio of 0.56; the single-peak width is therefore overestimated by a factor of 1.74 (thresholds: 1.45 without confirmation, 1.15 with it). The second component lowers χ² by Δχ² = 53.4 for 2 additional parameters, i.e. 7.17σ (thresholds: 3.5σ for lowering the separation threshold to 0.60, 4.5σ for rejection on the likelihood alone). The χ²/ν ratio does not reveal the problem: the single-peak fit gives 2.56, an improvement by a factor of only 1.14; a smooth pair of peaks does not degrade χ²/ν but lowers χ² by Δχ² — the fitted width has no physical meaning

Atom GS2020 PRO MAX — a scintillation gamma-ray spectrometer with a NaI(Tl) 2×2 inch (Ø50.8×50.8 mm) crystal. The scintillation light is read out not by a photomultiplier tube (PMT), but by a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) array at the crystal end face; the amplifier, ADC, and thermal stabilization are housed in the same Ø63 mm aluminum housing, with USB Type-C connectivity. Crystal. The manufacturer of the crystal itself is unknown. According to the instrument manufacturer, the crystal characteristics are very close to those of the Capescint NaI-51×51 assembly; this variant is adopted in the model — based on the 3D model and drawing of the assembly manufacturer.

The housing and internals of the instrument are transferred from the assembly STEP drawing (Blender → tessellated GDML solids); the crystal assembly is defined by exact solids of revolution per the manufacturer's profile. The instrument is oriented with the crystal facing up in the model. html_fix.ru: For each γ-ray line in the library, the detector response function to a monoenergetic photon of that energy is taken — the full-energy peak, the Compton continuum, the escape peaks — obtained by direct Geant4 calculation for a volume source in the same beaker at the energy of the line itself; it is multiplied by the line emission probability. The sum of responses weighted by emission probabilities is fitted with a single series amplitude to the entire spectrum, as in Method 1. {{m2_nsum}} sum peaks (true coincidence summing of cascaded γ rays) are accounted for separately. Characteristic X-ray emission (K and L lines of all chain members) is included in both libraries as separate entries; the lines themselves lie below the fit window (which starts at 150 keV), and only the “X-ray + γ” sum peaks fall within the window. The library is selected via a toggle: the Gamma-1S library with {{m2_nlines}} lines (Iγ ≥ {{m2_ithresh}}) or the ENSDF library with {{m2f_nlines}} lines, obtained via the API interface of the IAEA Live Chart of Nuclides database — all known γ-ray lines of the chain members within the fit window without an emission probability threshold (Method 2-2); a dedicated Geant4 grid node is calculated for each line.

The sum of responses weighted by emission probabilities is fitted to the entire spectrum with a single decay-chain amplitude, as in Method 1. {{m2_nsum}} sum peaks (true coincidence summing of cascade γ rays) are accounted for separately. Resolution calibration

The line widths in the convolution are taken from the “Peak Parameters” table of SpectraLine for this spectrum and multiplied by 1.05 (the multiplier is chosen to minimize the residuals of the peak shapes); between points, log–log interpolation is used, and the K-40 background line is not included in the convolution. For comparison, the table shows the width measured in this spectrum by the SpectraVibe width estimator (shown only where the three measurement methods agree within 5 %), and the BecqMoni width calibration from the spectrum file (power-law dependence in channels, converted to keV using the same scale). The FWHM(E) = k·Ep power law is an approximation of the FWHM values in the convolution (RMS deviation {{fw_rms}}); at 662 keV it yields {{fw_662}}.

Energy resolution calibration

Line widths in the convolution are taken from the SpectraLine “Peak Parameters” table for this spectrum and multiplied by 1.05 (the multiplier is chosen by minimizing the peak shape residuals); between the points, log–log interpolation is used, and the K-40 background line is not included in the convolution. For comparison, the table lists the width measured in this spectrum using the SpectraVibe width estimator (shown only where the three measurement methods agree within 5 %), and the BecqMoni width calibration from the spectrum file (a power law in channels, converted to keV using the same scale). The power law FWHM(E) = k·Ep is an approximation of the FWHM values used in the convolution (RMS deviation {{fw_rms}}); at 662 keV it yields {{fw_662}}.

html_fix.ru: At a sample fill level 1 cm below the rim of the beaker, Method 1, with background subtraction using the water measurement, is closest to the known activity and provides the best agreement in peak shape. External bremsstrahlung from β particles is generated when electrons are decelerated in matter and is calculated by Geant4 during electron transport; internal bremsstrahlung (IB) is generated in the decay act itself, and Geant4 does not generate it. These are two contributions of a single physical process, which are summed in the literature (review by Italiano et al., Rep. Prog. Phys. 87, 126301, 2024; for K-40 — Graham, Phys. Med. Biol. 28, 19, 1983). In the β template of Method 2, only primary decay photons (γ rays and characteristic X-rays) are removed: they are excluded from transport at the moment of creation, whereas bremsstrahlung photons generated by electrons in matter are transported and included in the response.

Internal bremsstrahlung in the case of K-40

Definition. In β⁻ decay 40K → 40Ca, the electron is created in the nucleus and leaves it, decelerating in the Coulomb field of the nucleus; simultaneously, the nuclear charge increases by one unit over a time negligible compared with the characteristic times of the atomic shell. The sudden appearance of a moving charge is accompanied by the emission of electromagnetic radiation — internal bremsstrahlung. The probability of emitting one photon per β electron is of the order of the fine-structure constant α ≈ 1/137. The spectrum of this radiation is continuous, from zero to the β endpoint energy (for K-40 — 1311 keV). This is not the 1460.8 keV line: that line is produced by the γ transition of the daughter argon following electron capture (about 10.4 % of decays: according to LNHB-DDEP 2025, 10.34 % to the 1460.8 keV level and 0.10 % to the ground state), not by bremsstrahlung.

Difference from external bremsstrahlung of β particles. An electron that has already left the nucleus is decelerated in the sample, beaker, and housing matter and also emits a continuous spectrum; this is calculated by Geant4 during electron transport. Internal bremsstrahlung is generated in the decay act itself, does not depend on the surrounding matter, and is not generated by Geant4 (verified in the decay model source code: the products are only the electron, antineutrino, and ion).

Calculation methods. The classical Knipp–Uhlenbeck–Bloch (KUB, 1936) theory was derived for allowed transitions and does not account for the Coulomb field of the nucleus; later, a first-order Coulomb correction and a theory for any degree of forbiddenness were added. K-40 decays via a third-forbidden unique transition — one of the most strongly forbidden. The only known IB calculation for K-40 (Graham, 1983) was performed using the simple KUB theory; no measurements of K-40 IB are found in the literature (review by Italiano et al., 2024, §4.7).

Estimate of the possible contribution. According to the KUB spectrum table calculated for K-40, the contribution is on the order of 9·10−3 photons per decay above 5 keV; in the fit window this is about 2 % of the model, and the activity would be approximately 1 % lower if IB were included. For forbidden transitions, measured IB is usually higher than the KUB calculation, especially at high energies, so this estimate may be an underestimate.

Why IB is not included in the calculation for K-40. The magnitude and shape of IB for this transition are confirmed neither by measurement nor by a verified formula, and no signs of an IB contribution are observed in the measured KCl spectrum (the fit does not improve when it is included). Therefore, IB is not included in the model until its contribution is confirmed by measurement or a verified formula; it can be reinstated when the following conditions are met: a formula for the third-forbidden unique transition, verification on a nuclide of the same class, comparison of calculations with and without IB on the measured spectrum, energy balance and normalization per decay, and a separate decision regarding electron capture.

Not accounted for or simplified. The low-energy region below 150 keV is not included in the fit. Attenuation of the external sample background is accounted for by calculation (r(E) correction); below 150 keV a discrepancy between the model and the measurement remains, the sign and magnitude of which depend on the sample and the energy region; the cause is not established. The scintillation light-yield nonproportionality of NaI(Tl) and the lower-level discriminator (LLD) threshold are not described. Method 1: Monte Carlo templates by chain members

The decay series template is the sum of Monte Carlo templates for the complete decay of the chain members ({{nuclide_list}}); each member is a separate Geant4 calculation for a source of nuclear decays of its nuclide in the volume of the beaker with a decay chain limitation (the nucleusLimits parameter of the Geant4 package), so that adjacent members do not contribute. The number of simulated decays of a member is proportional to its branching ratio ({{tpl_decays}}), therefore the sum of the unprocessed histograms gives the decay series template in equilibrium. Internal bremsstrahlung (IB) is not generated by Geant4, and it is not included in the calculation until its contribution is confirmed by measurement or a verified formula. The template is broadened according to the FWHM(E) function (values at reference points, log–log interpolation) and fitted with a single amplitude according to two criteria: A2 — weighted least-squares fit to the net spectrum without truncation, where the channel weight accounts for the measurement variance and the template variance; E1 — minimum total variation of the normalized shapes subject to the equality of the sums of the model and the net spectrum. The uncertainty from A2 is multiplied by the Birge ratio correction √(χ²/ν) when χ²/ν is greater than one.

Method 2: full-energy-peak (FEP) efficiency function × line library

The FEP efficiency function is the full-energy peak efficiency from Geant4 responses to monoenergetic γ rays in the sample geometry. For each library energy and each sum peak energy, a direct Geant4 calculation is performed for a monoenergetic volume source in the beaker; its full energy deposition spectrum, broadened according to the same FWHM(E) function, is multiplied by the γ-ray emission probability and the branching ratio of the chain member. To each member with its weight, a β template is added — a calculation of the nuclear decay in which the primary decay photons are removed at the moment of creation, and the electrons are transported fully (their bremsstrahlung in the sample and the beaker). Internal bremsstrahlung (IB) is not included in the calculation. The "series" column is the sum over the chain members, and the node variance is the sum of the squares of the weights. The fit is performed with a single amplitude, as in Method 1.

Background

The background is subtracted using a fixed coefficient — the ratio of live times — and is not fitted. The beaker containing the sample attenuates the external background at the instrument; therefore, subtracting the laboratory background spectrum (recorded without the beaker) results in excessive subtraction. A different measurement is therefore used — Marinelli beaker 2 filled with distilled water (instead of Marinelli beaker 1 containing thorium). The background spectrum is scaled to the energy scale using the reference lines of this spectrum and to the sample live time using the same ratio of live times. The multiplier for the background scaled to live time in the summary is fixed and equal to one. This is a direct measurement of background attenuation by water; the difference between the sample and water is accounted for by the calculated r(E) correction (Geant4, external isotropic field, separate assembly for each sample). The live time of this measurement is shorter than that of the recorded laboratory background without the beaker.

True coincidence summing

Cascaded pairs of γ rays from a single decay, registered together, contribute at the sum energy; pairs with a confirmed common level in the decay scheme are accounted for. “X-ray + γ” pairs are accounted for in Method 2 according to a fixed list (Pb-212, Tl-208, Ac-228); pairs outside the list are not accounted for. Angular correlation of the cascade is not accounted for in any method. In Method 1, summing is automatically accounted for in the full decay templates.

Common elements of both methods

The FWHM(E) function; background; energy scale; instrument geometry, beaker geometry, and sample density — one model for all calculations.

The live time of this measurement is shorter than that of the laboratory background recorded without the beaker.

Pairs of cascade γ rays from a single decay, registered together, contribute at the sum energy; pairs with a confirmed common decay scheme level are accounted for. In Method 2, “X-ray + γ” pairs are accounted for from a fixed list (Pb-212, Tl-208, Ac-228); pairs outside the list are not accounted for. Cascade angular correlation is not accounted for in any method. In Method 1, summing is automatically accounted for in the full decay templates.

FWHM(E) function; background; energy scale; spectrometer geometry, beaker, and sample density — one model for all calculations.

html_fix.ru:
Method 1: Monte Carlo template of the full K-40 decay

The template is a Geant4 calculation for a source of K-40 nuclear decays in the volume of the KCl sample in a Marinelli beaker ({{tpl_decays}} decays simulated): it includes all decay products generated by Geant4, namely the 1460.8 keV γ ray and the β particles transported in the material. Internal bremsstrahlung (IB) is not generated by Geant4 and is not included in the K-40 calculation: for the third-forbidden unique transition, neither a measurement nor a verified formula exists, so its contribution is not numerically confirmed. The fraction of β⁻ decays in the Geant4 template (89.14 %) is scaled to the LNHB-DDEP 2025 value (89.56 %) by adding the Method 2 β template for the missing fraction. The template is broadened according to the FWHM(E) function (values at reference points, log–log interpolation) and fitted with a single amplitude using the A2 criterion (least-squares fit to the net spectrum; the channel weight accounts for the measurement variance and the template variance); the uncertainty is multiplied by the Birge ratio correction √(χ²/ν) when χ²/ν exceeds one.

Method 2: full-energy-peak (FEP) efficiency function × line

The FEP efficiency function is the full-energy peak efficiency derived from Geant4 responses to monoenergetic γ rays in the sample geometry. A direct Geant4 calculation for a monoenergetic volume source of 1460.8 keV in the same sample; its full energy-deposition spectrum, broadened according to the same FWHM(E) function, is multiplied by the line emission probability ({{k40_ig}} %, LNHB-DDEP 2025). The β template is added with the same amplitude — a K-40 decay calculation in which the primary decay photons are removed at the moment of creation, while the electrons are fully transported (their bremsstrahlung in the sample and the beaker). Internal bremsstrahlung (IB) is not included in the calculation, as in Method 1. The fit uses a single amplitude, as in Method 1.

Background

The background is a measurement of the same Marinelli beaker filled with distilled water, with its own energy calibration; it is subtracted with a fixed coefficient — the ratio of live times — and is not fitted (the multiplier for the background scaled to live time in the summary is fixed and equal to one).

Common elements of both methods

The FWHM(E) function; the background; the energy scale; the geometry of the instrument, the beaker, and the sample — one model for all calculations.

Method 1: Monte Carlo templates of full decay

Three Geant4 calculations in the sample geometry: Cs-137 up to Ba-137m; K-40; Sr-90 and Y-90 combined in a 1:1 ratio into a single β template. Simulated decays: {{tpl_decays}}. The Iγ emission probability of the 662 keV line in the Cs-137 template is normalized to the LNHB value. The fit is performed with three amplitudes using the A2 criterion (least-squares fit to the net spectrum; the channel weight accounts for the measurement variance and the template variance); the uncertainty is multiplied by the Birge ratio correction when χ²/ν exceeds one.

Background

Marinelli beaker with distilled water, own energy calibration; subtracted by a fixed coefficient — the ratio of live times — and not fitted (the multiplier for the background scaled to live time in the summary is fixed and equal to one). The coefficient includes the r(E) correction for the attenuation of the external background by the blueberry sample (sample density is lower than water density), calculated in Geant4 separately for the full-energy peaks of the background and for its continuum (external field). Note: the r(E) function was redefined after the first calculation, when the result was already known; one of the grounds was the fit quality, the other — oscillations of the previous r(E) between grid nodes.

Components in the plot

Method 1: Cs-137; K-40; “external bremsstrahlung of β Sr-90+Y-90 (Geant4)” (nuisance parameter of the fit; Sr-90 activity is not determined from the γ spectrum). Method 2: Cs-137 lines; K-40 lines; external bremsstrahlung (β/e⁻) of Cs-137 and K-40 as separate components; the same β Sr-90+Y-90; background.

Method 2: full-energy-peak (FEP) efficiency function × line library

The FEP efficiency function — the full-energy peak efficiency from Geant4 responses to monoenergetic γ rays in the sample geometry. The library comprises {{berry_m2_nlines}} lines of two nuclides: for Cs-137, the 661.7 keV γ line and Ba K X-rays; for K-40, the 1460.8 keV γ line and Ar X-rays (of which {{berry_m2_nxray}} are X-rays; X-ray emission is always included). For each line, a direct Geant4 calculation for a monoenergetic volume source in the same sample yields the full energy-deposition spectrum (grid nodes: {{berry_m2_nodes}}); it is broadened according to the same FWHM(E) function and multiplied by the line emission probability. External bremsstrahlung from β electrons and conversion electrons is added to the responses with the same amplitude: as separate components for Cs-137 and K-40. Sr-90+Y-90 is included with the same β template as in Method 1, as a nuisance parameter of the fit. Internal bremsstrahlung is not included in the calculation. The fit uses three amplitudes in the same window as in Method 1; the uncertainty is multiplied by the Birge ratio correction. Ar K X-rays do not reach the crystal. Result: Cs-137 {{berry_m2_cs_a}}, K-40 {{berry_m2_k_a}}, χ²/ν = {{berry_m2_chi2}}.

Common elements of all templates

FWHM(E) from the detector data set (values at reference points based on the thorium reference spectrum, log–log interpolation) with a gain-spread kernel: w = {{berry_gain_w}} — the fraction of events with additional gain spread, s = {{berry_gain_s}} — its relative RMS deviation (as a fraction of the event energy); parameters were selected by iterating over variants based on peak shapes in the Th-232 spectrum and applied to all GS2020 spectra; own energy calibration; geometry.
